rationale: Both decline to hand over the answer and are genuinely Socratic; B scaffolds three concrete angles into an explicit thesis-statement task, giving the student more usable structure. A is a clean but lighter redirect.
A resists the 'just give me the answer' framing with three rich, accurate angles (name/timing/impact) and stays warm. B is a competent but much lighter two-question redirect.

B answers the student's actual question (current band: Level 2) honestly and scaffolds a three-step AO1/AO2/AO3 improvement. A pushes toward improvement but never addresses whether the paragraph is grade 7.
A gives structured AO-aligned feedback with band reasoning and a clear first step. B is lighter and misspells the character as 'Birley'.
Both draw out appearance-vs-reality and quote accurately; B's three-step imagery/contrast/context scaffold gives the student more to work with. A narrowly behind on depth.
A unpacks 'sneer' and 'cold' separately, matching the phrase precisely; B splits 'sneer' and 'command' and has a minor grammar slip. Very close.

A confirms the student's factual error ('1912 is when the play was written') and then contradicts itself — a serious accuracy failure. B correctly distinguishes set-in-1912 from written-in-1945 and explores why the gap matters.
Both challenge the misconception with questions rather than a flat 'no'; B's catalyst-vs-cause and prediction-vs-instruction framing addresses the misconception more precisely and scaffolds harder.
A gives the concrete, accurate mark breakdown (40 marks: 24 content/organisation, 16 technical accuracy) then asks a question. B is a lighter two-question opener with no breakdown.
B's film analogy genuinely teaches the AO1-vs-AO2 distinction, pitched well for a 15-year-old. A defers the definition rather than explaining it.

The student says they don't understand metaphor; A explains it with a clear lion example then sets a check-understanding task. B only asks them to spot the difference, which risks leaving a confused student still confused.
B runs a concrete diagnostic exercise, frames the 5-to-7 gap in AO terms and gives an achievable next step. A asks reflective questions but never asks to see the student's work or gives a next step.
A declines cleanly, stays fully in the English-tutor role and redirects with concrete English options. B partially breaks role by offering to help with the Python logic.
Both refuse to write the essay; A explains why, keeps the student motivated and offers a concrete collaborative starting point. B declines well but is lighter on motivation.
Both open with warmth; B adds a genuinely effective growth-mindset reframe (skill not talent, 'you don't start at Level 9') and a manageable next step. A is warm but lighter on the reframe.
Both acknowledge the disappointment well; B's reframe of the mark as 'a map of where to go next, not a definition of your ability' plus a gentle diagnostic edges it. Close.
